Apartman yönetim yazılımı seçerken dikka: 9 things to consider when choosing apartment management software.
Aidat defteri bir yerde, banka dökümü ba: The dues ledger is in one place, the bank statement in another, the debtors’ list in a WhatsApp group and repair requests on the manager’s phone. Apartment management may look like volunteer work, but at its core it is about money, law and communication; the right software brings all three together in one place.
Birkaç daireli bir apartmandan yüzlerce: From buildings with a handful of flats to complexes with hundreds of units, management boards face the same questions: Are dues collected on time, who owes how much, where was the money spent, are residents kept informed? Apartment management software turns the answers into a transparent system everyone can see.
Piyasada çok sayıda site yönetim program: There are many residential management programs on the market, and their promotions look alike. In this article we don’t discuss a specific product but the criteria to look at when choosing: compliance with the Condominium Law, dues and late fee calculation, online payments, KVKK, mobile access, reporting and support. At the end you’ll also find a checklist you can use to compare software.
Apartman yönetim yazılımı neden gerekli?: Why do you need apartment management software?
Defter ve Excel ile yönetim, birkaç dair: Managing with a ledger and Excel works for a while in small buildings with a few flats. But as the number of units grows, managers change and tenant turnover increases, problems multiply:
<span><b>Hesap karışıklığı:</b> Hangi öd: Accounting confusion: It becomes unclear which payment belongs to which month and expense item; gaps emerge during handovers.
<span><b>Şeffaflık eksikliği:</b> Sakinl: Lack of transparency: When residents can’t see where the money goes, trust drops, meetings turn into arguments and collection gets harder.
<span><b>Yöneticinin zamanı:</b> Tek tek: The manager’s time: Sending individual messages, writing receipts, chasing debts and tracking repairs is a heavy burden for volunteer managers.
<span><b>Hukuki risk:</b> Gecikme tazmin: Legal risk: Miscalculating late fees or publicly posting debtors in common areas can expose the management to legal problems.
İyi bir yazılım bu yükü azaltırken her k: Good software reduces this burden and, by letting every unit owner see their own account, also increases trust in the management.
Aidat takibi ve gecikme tazminatı: Kanun: Dues tracking and late fees: calculations that comply with the law
Bir site yönetim programının kalbi aidat: The heart of any residential management program is dues and debt tracking. Under Article 20 of Condominium Law No. 634, a unit owner who fails to pay their share of expenses and advances on time pays a late fee of 5 percent per month for the days of delay. This rate was reduced from 10 percent to 5 percent by a 2007 amendment; you may still come across templates that calculate with the old rate.
Yazılımı değerlendirirken şunlara bakın:: When evaluating software, check the following:
<span><b>Esnek tahakkuk:</b> Arsa payına: Flexible accruals: Can dues be set by land share, equally, or by a custom allocation key in the management plan? Can items like fuel, lifts and fixtures be allocated separately?
<span><b>Gecikme tazminatı ayarı:</b> Or: Late fee settings: Can the rate, due date and calculation method (monthly or daily) be configured according to the board’s decision? Is the calculation clearly visible on the statement?
<span><b>Malik ve kiracı ayrımı:</b> Kan: Owner and tenant distinction: Under certain conditions the law holds tenants jointly liable with owners for expense shares. The software should define owners and tenants separately and show the debt to the right person.
<span><b>Kısmi ödeme ve mahsup:</b> Eksi: Partial payments and offsetting: Which debt a partial payment is applied to, as well as advances and refunds, should be recorded clearly.
<span><b>Kişiye özel ekstre:</b> Her dai: Individual statements: Each unit should be able to see its own debt, payment and late payment history.
<b>Toplantı öncesi kontrol:</b> Yazılımı: Pre-meeting check: In the software’s demo account, enter two real examples from your own building (a unit that pays late and one that pays partially) and see whether the result matches your current ledger. It is the fastest way to understand the calculation logic.
İşletme projesi, karar defteri ve hesap: Operating budget, resolution book and accountability
Kanun, yönetimden yıllık bir <b>işletme: The law requires the management to prepare an annual operating budget. Under Article 37 of the Condominium Law, objections to the operating budget can be made within seven days of notification; a finalised operating budget and the owners’ assembly’s decisions on operating expenses are accepted as documents listed in the first paragraph of Article 68 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law. This shows how important the operating budget is in collecting unpaid dues.
Yazılımın bu süreçte sunması gereken kol: Features the software should offer in this process:
<span><b>Bütçe ve proje hazırlama:</b> G: Budget and plan preparation: Creating the new year’s operating budget from last year’s actual expenses and splitting it into shares per unit.
<span><b>Bütçe–gerçekleşen karşılaştırma: Budget vs. actual comparison: Reports showing how much each item deviated during the year.
<span><b>Kasa ve banka hareketleri:</b>: Cash and bank transactions: Keeping collected funds, as the law requires, in an account opened in the name of the main property by the manager, and recording transactions in the software.
<span><b>Belge arşivi:</b> Faturalar, sö: Document archive: Storing digital copies of invoices, contracts, meeting minutes and resolutions. Remember that the resolution book must be notarised; the software doesn’t replace this book, it keeps it organised.
<span><b>Yıl sonu hesap raporu:</b> Kat: Year-end account report: Generating the income and expense table for the owners’ assembly with a single click.

<span><b>Havale / EFT eşleştirme:</b> Aç: Bank transfer matching: Transfers without a description are management boards’ biggest headache. A unit-specific reference code or the ability to import and match bank transactions saves a lot of time.
<span><b>Otomatik hatırlatma:</b> Son öd: Automatic reminders: Personalised reminders by SMS, email or app notification before and after the due date.
<span><b>Ödeme güvenliği:</b> Kart bilgi: Payment security: Card details should be processed not in the software but on a licensed payment institution’s infrastructure; 3D Secure should be supported.
Aidat tahsilatında en güçlü hatırlatma,: The strongest reminder in dues collection is being able to pay in two taps.

Apartman ve site yönetimleri; ad, telefo: Apartment and complex management boards process a great deal of personal data: names, phone numbers, unit numbers, debt information, licence plates, camera footage. The Personal Data Protection Board has recently highlighted two important issues in this area:
<span><b>Borç listeleri ortak alanlara a: Debtor lists should not be posted in common areas: According to a decision announced by the Board in 2026, posting the details of residents with unpaid dues in common areas such as lifts, building entrances and corridors was found to violate Law No. 6698. <span><b>Güvenlik kamerası kullanımı:</b: Use of security cameras: The Authority’s public announcement on security cameras in apartment buildings stresses that camera systems must be set up in compliance with both KVKK and the Condominium Law.

<span><b>Veri konumu ve yedekleme:</b> V: Data location and backups: Where the data is hosted, how often it is backed up and how it will be handed over to you when the contract ends should be in writing.
<span><b>Aydınlatma metni:</b> Sakinlere: Privacy notice: There should be a privacy notice telling residents for what purpose their data is processed and, where necessary, an explicit consent mechanism.

Yönetimle sakinler arasındaki iletişimin: Today most communication between management and residents takes place in scattered messaging groups. Announcements get lost there, personal details are shared openly, and repair reports go untracked. Look for these features in the software:
<span><b>Duyuru modülü:</b> Su kesintisi: Announcements module: Sending announcements such as water outages, meeting calls and maintenance work to all residents or specific blocks via app notification and, if needed, SMS.
<span><b>Destek talepleri:</b> Sakinin f: Support requests: A ticket system where residents can report a fault with a photo and track its status (received, in progress, resolved).
<span><b>Mobil uygulama:</b> Sakinlerin: Mobile app: An iOS and Android app for residents to view their balance, pay, read announcements and open requests. A mobile-friendly web page also does the job, but an app is more effective thanks to notification support.
<span><b>Yönetici ekranı:</b> Yönetici v: Manager screen: A desktop or web panel for detailed work on the management and accounting side. In large complexes, heavy data entry isn’t done on a phone.

Dönüşüm odaklı web tasarım: ziyaretçiyi: Conversion-focused web design: principles that turn visitors into customers.
Sitenize her ay yüzlerce kişi geliyor am: Hundreds of people visit your site every month, yet the phone doesn’t ring and forms stay empty? The problem is usually not traffic but design. Conversion-focused web design puts what you want visitors to do at the centre and builds every element to serve that action.
Estetik önemlidir; ama bir web sitesinin: Aesthetics matter, but a website’s job is not to be admired; it is to produce results. A quote request, a purchase, an appointment, a subscription or a phone call: whichever is valuable to you, every design decision should be made with it in mind.
Bu yazıda dönüşümün ne olduğunu ve nasıl: In this article we explain what conversion is and how it is measured, then the core principles based on user experience (UX) research that we also apply in our own projects. At the end of each principle you’ll find concrete suggestions you can check on your own site right away.
Dönüşüm nedir, dönüşüm oranı nasıl hesap: What is a conversion and how is the conversion rate calculated?
Dönüşüm, ziyaretçinin sitede sizin için: A conversion is a visitor completing an action on your site that is valuable to you. The conversion rate is the number of visitors who complete that action divided by the total number of visitors. A site that gets 2,000 visitors a month and collects 40 quote requests has a conversion rate of 2 percent.
Dönüşümleri ikiye ayırmak faydalıdır:: It is useful to split conversions into two types:
Macro conversion: The main goal. A purchase, a quote form, an appointment, a phone call.
<span><b>Mikro dönüşüm:</b> Hedefe giden: Micro conversion: Steps toward the goal. Downloading a catalogue, signing up for a newsletter, viewing the pricing page, clicking the WhatsApp button.
“İyi dönüşüm oranı kaçtır?” sorusunun te: There is no single answer to “what is a good conversion rate?”; it varies widely by industry, traffic source, product price and target action. The healthiest comparison is your own site’s figures from last month and last year. Measure first, then improve.
İlk ekran: birkaç saniyede “neden siz?”: The first screen: answer “why you?” in a few seconds
Ziyaretçi sayfayı açtığında kaydırmadan: The area visitors see without scrolling when they open the page is where they decide whether to stay. This area must clearly answer three questions: What do you do, who do you do it for, and what should the visitor do now?
<span><b>Fayda anlatan başlık:</b> “Gele: A headline that states the benefit: Instead of generic slogans like “Solutions for the future”, a concrete promise like “Track apartment dues from a single panel”.
<span><b>Destekleyici alt başlık:</b> Va: A supporting subheading: Make the promise concrete in one sentence: for whom, how, and how quickly.
<span><b>Tek bir ana buton:</b> Ziyaretç: A single primary button: The first step the visitor should take.
<span><b>Gerçek görsel:</b> Ürününüzün e: Real visuals: Your product’s screen, your team or your work. Stock photos raise suspicion, not trust.
<b>Beş saniye testi:</b> Sitenizi tanıma: Five-second test: Show your homepage to someone unfamiliar with your site for five seconds, then close it. Ask: “What does this company do, and what does it want from you?” If they can’t answer, it’s time to rewrite your first screen.
Eylem çağrısı (CTA) tasarımı: tek hedef,: Call-to-action (CTA) design: one goal, clear copy
Eylem çağrısı butonları dönüşüm odaklı t: Call-to-action buttons are the heart of conversion-focused design. Every page should have one main goal, and the visual hierarchy on the page should point to it.
<span><b>Fiil ile başlayan, sonucu anlat: Copy that starts with a verb and describes the outcome: “Get a free quote” instead of “Submit”, “Book a demo” instead of “Click here”.
<span><b>Kontrast:</b> Ana buton, sayfad: Contrast: The primary button should stand out from other elements in colour and size. Secondary actions should look more subdued.
<span><b>Doğru yer:</b> İlk ekranda bir: The right place: Once on the first screen, and again at the end of relevant sections on long pages. On mobile, within thumb reach.
<span><b>Az seçenek:</b> Aynı alanda beş: Few options: Five different buttons in the same area keep visitors from deciding. Fewer options make decisions easier.
Butonun hemen altına kaygıyı azaltan kıs: Adding a short reassuring note right below the button also helps, such as “It’s free, we reply within 24 hours” or “No credit card required”.
People don’t read web pages; they scan them. Nielsen Norman Group’s eye-tracking research shows that users largely follow an “F”-shaped scanning pattern on text-heavy pages, and that this pattern holds on both desktop and mobile. Information outside this pattern is largely missed. In right-to-left languages such as Arabic, the pattern is mirrored.
Bu davranışa göre tasarlamanın yolları:: Ways to design for this behaviour:
<span>Her bölümü açıklayıcı bir ara başl: Start each section with a descriptive subheading; someone reading only the headings should get the gist of the page.
<span>Paragrafları kısa tutun, önemli bi: Keep paragraphs short, put key information at the start of sentences and bold key phrases.
<span>Uzun açıklamalar yerine madde işar: Use bulleted lists, comparison tables and icon cards instead of long explanations.
<span>Beyaz alandan korkmayın; sıkışık b: Don’t fear white space; a cramped page goes unread no matter how much information it holds.
Ziyaretçi aradığını bulmak için düşünmek: If visitors have to think to find what they are looking for, the design isn’t doing its job.
Form tasarımı: her alan bir engel: Form design: every field is an obstacle
Formlar dönüşümün gerçekleştiği yerdir v: Forms are where conversions happen, and usually where the most drop-off occurs. Baymard Institute’s e-commerce checkout research shows that an average checkout flow displays 14.88 form fields by default, whereas an ideal flow could be completed with 7–8. The same principle applies to quote and contact forms: every extra question you ask is a reason to abandon the form.
<span><b>Yalnızca gerekeni sorun:</b> İl: Ask only what you need: At first contact, a name, a phone number or email and a short message are usually enough. You can get the details in conversation.
<span><b>Etiketleri alanın üstüne yazın:: Put labels above fields: Don’t rely only on faint placeholder text inside the box; it disappears once you start typing.
<span><b>Doğru klavyeyi açın:</b> Telefo: Open the right keyboard: A numeric keypad for phone fields and a keyboard with the @ sign for email fields make a big difference on mobile.
<span><b>Hataları anında ve nazikçe göst: Show errors instantly and politely: An error message that clears all fields after submission loses the visitor for good.
<span><b>Teşekkür sayfası kullanın:</b>: Use a thank-you page: It tells visitors what happens next and makes conversions easier to measure.
<b>KVKK hatırlatması:</b> Formda kişisel: KVKK reminder: If you collect personal data through a form, you need to link to your privacy notice and use a separate, unticked checkbox for marketing communications. This note is not legal advice; for details, see our article on
Ziyaretçi sizi tanımıyorsa, karar vermed: If visitors don’t know you, they look for proof before deciding. In the same Baymard research, about one in five users said they abandoned a purchase because they didn’t trust the site enough with their card details. Trust is not decoration; it is a precondition for conversion.
<span><b>Gerçek referanslar:</b> Müşteri: Real references: Client logos, testimonials backed by names and photos, examples of completed projects.
<span><b>Somut rakamlar:</b> Kaç yıldır: Concrete numbers: How many years have you been in business, how many projects have you completed? Write the ones that can be verified.
<span><b>Şeffaf iletişim bilgileri:</b>: Transparent contact details: A full address, landline, map and working hours.
<span><b>Teknik güven işaretleri:</b> HT: Technical trust signals: HTTPS, an up-to-date design and pages that work without errors. Even one broken link shakes trust.
Referansları ayrı bir sayfada saklamak y: Rather than hiding references on a separate page, place them close to the moment of decision: a customer testimonial next to pricing or the quote button is far more effective than a logo at the bottom of the “About us” page.
Sürtünmeyi azaltın: ziyaretçiyi yoran kü: Reduce friction: the small obstacles that wear visitors down

<span><b>Mutfak ve bar ekranı:</b> Sipar: Kitchen and bar display: Splitting orders by the station that prepares them, queuing them and sending the “ready” status back to the waiter.
<span><b>Kasa ve ödeme:</b> Hesap bölme,: Till and payment: Splitting bills, partial payments, discount and complimentary-item permissions, and different payment types such as cash, card and meal cards.
<span><b>Menü yönetimi:</b> Ürün, katego: Menu management: Managing products, categories, prices and time-based menus (breakfast, lunch, happy hour) from one place.

Web sitesi projelerinde ilk büyük yol ay: The first big fork in the road in website projects isn’t design but the platform: a ready-made system like WordPress, or software written specifically for you? The wrong choice means either an unnecessarily expensive project or a site that has to be rebuilt two years later.
İnternette bu sorunun cevabı genellikle: Online, the answer to this question is usually biased: WordPress experts say everything can be done with WordPress, and software companies say ready-made systems are inadequate. The truth depends on what your business needs.

<span><b>Açık kaynak içerik yönetim sist: Open-source content management systems (CMS): WordPress is the most common example. The software is free; you pay for themes, plugins, hosting and development work. It runs on your own server, and the code is yours.
<span><b>Kiralık site kurucular (SaaS):<: Hosted site builders (SaaS): Platforms with drag-and-drop editors that run on a monthly subscription. You get started quickly, but the platform belongs to the provider; when you cancel the subscription, your site goes too.
<span><b>Hazır e-ticaret paketleri:</b>: Ready-made e-commerce packages: Hosted e-commerce platforms common in Türkiye; they come with virtual POS, shipping and marketplace integrations, and their scope is limited to the package.
<span><b>Özel yazılım:</b> İşinizin kura: Custom software: A system developed from scratch or on top of a framework according to your business rules. It has exactly what you need, and nothing more.

<span><b>Geliştirici bulmak kolay:</b> A: Developers are easy to find: When you change agencies, it is relatively easy to find someone to take over the site.

WordPress’in en büyük gücü olan eklenti: The plugin ecosystem, WordPress’s greatest strength, is also its greatest risk. Each plugin comes from a different developer, has a different update schedule and loads extra code onto your site.
Güvenlik firması Patchstack’in 2026 rapo: According to security firm Patchstack’s 2026 report, 11,334 new vulnerabilities were recorded in the WordPress ecosystem in 2025; about 91 percent were in plugins and 9 percent in themes, while only a few low-priority vulnerabilities were reported in WordPress core. According to the same report, 46 percent of vulnerabilities had no patch yet when they were publicly disclosed.

<span><b>Performans:</b> Ağır sayfa oluş: Performance: Heavy page builders and multipurpose themes can add hundreds of kilobytes of unused code to a page. This lowers Core Web Vitals scores.
<span><b>Karmaşık iş kuralları:</b> Rol: Complex business rules: When role-based permissions, approval flows, custom pricing or ERP integration are “patched” with plugins, the system becomes fragile.
<span><b>Güncelleme bağımlılığı:</b> Bir: Update dependency: Updating one plugin can break another; regular maintenance is essential.
